To determine the truthfulness of each statement regarding fixed-rate mortgages (FRM) and adjustable-rate mortgages (ARM):

This statement is incorrect. ### Option (C): "Using an ARM can lead to higher total interest costs over the life of the loan compared to a FRM, depending on market conditions."
This statement is true. If interest rates decline over the life of the ARM, the borrower could end up paying less in total interest compared to an FRM. Conversely, if interest rates rise, the total interest paid over the life of the loan could exceed that of an FRM. Thus, the total cost depends on market fluctuations.

**Conclusion:** Only statement (C) is true.
